commands.author: Pick-cat

target.title: fix(codex): reject hex/exponent computer wait duration strings
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex computer `wait` / `hold_key` outer watchdog deadlines used JavaScript `Number(...)` on free-form `duration` values. Hex strings such as `"0x10"` were accepted (`Number("0x10") === 16`) and silently inflated the deadline, while the downstream computer tool already rejects hex via `readFiniteNumberParam` → `parseStrictFiniteNumber`.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Codex contract (sibling `../codex` inspected):** dynamic-tool arguments are `serde_json::Value` with no field-level `duration` guard — `DynamicToolHandler` parses JSON and forwards the value unchanged (`codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs:136`, checkout `bdd282f3bbd55df3a869a5438519cd948c134d4d`). OpenClaw pins `@openai/codex@0.144.4`.

**Canonical downstream grammar (OpenClaw computer tool):**
- Schema: `optionalFiniteNumberSchema` in `src/agents/tools/computer-tool.ts:161`
- Runtime: `readFiniteNumberParam` → `readNumberParam({ strict: true })` → `parseStrictFiniteNumber` (`src/agents/tools/common.ts:228`, `computer-tool.ts:856`)

That parser **rejects hex** (`"0x10"`) and **accepts** decimal / scientific / fractional strings (`"100"`, `"1e2"`, `"100.5"`, `"0.5"`) plus finite numbers.

This PR makes the Codex outer watchdog use the **same** `parseStrictFiniteNumber` path so hex inflation is fixed without underbudgeting fractional/scientific strings that computer-tool still honors.

Collision: overlaps [#107623](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107623); this head is the rebased, contract-aligned form.

## User Impact

| Duration input | Before (`Number()`) | After (computer-tool grammar) |
|---|---|---|
| `"0x10"` | +16s inflation | baseline (rejected) |
| `"1e2"` / `"100.5"` / `"0.5"` | coerced | honored (aligned) |
| `0.5` (number) | honored | honored |

## Evidence

Exact head: `d85b72dabe57770b68e901f974a448729cf05581`

### Call path

```
Codex app-server request
  → run-attempt-server-requests.ts:191  resolveDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs({ call, config })
    → dynamic-tool-execution.ts:499     readComputerToolTimeoutMs(value)
      → dynamic-tool-execution.ts:517   readComputerDurationMs(args.duration)
        → parseStrictFiniteNumber(value)   ← same grammar as computer-tool
```

The changed function `resolveDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs` is **the exact entry point** called from the real Codex app-server dynamic-tool request handler at `run-attempt-server-requests.ts:191`. No additional transformation or argument rewriting occurs between the Codex request and the timeout resolution.

### Format and diff check

```
$ git diff --check origin/main..HEAD && echo ok
ok
```

### Vitest suite — 30 tests covering all duration edge cases

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  30 passed (30)
```

The new test `"aligns computer duration strings with computer-tool parseStrictFiniteNumber"` exercises `resolveDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs` with real `computer` tool-call payloads — the exact call shape from `run-attempt-server-requests.ts:191`. It verifies:

| Input | Expected timeout | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `"0x10"` (hex) | 120_000ms | Rejected → baseline |
| `"1e2"` (scientific) | 250_000ms | Honored (100s) |
| `"100.5"` (fraction) | 220_500ms | Honored (100.5s) |
| `"0.5"` (fraction) | 120_500ms | Honored (0.5s) |
| `0.5` (numeric) | 120_500ms | Honored |
| `"100"` (decimal) | 220_000ms | Honored |

All 30 existing tests continue to pass — no regression.

### Mutation check

Revert `readComputerDurationMs` → `Number()`:
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts -t "aligns computer"

 FAIL  ... > aligns computer duration strings with computer-tool parseStrictFiniteNumber
AssertionError: expected 136000 to be 120000
    at extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts:251:12

 Tests  1 failed | 29 skipped (30)
```

`Number("0x10")` = 16 inflates the deadline to 136000ms instead of the expected 120000ms baseline. Restore `readComputerDurationMs` → 30/30 passed.

### Grammar alignment verification

`parseStrictFiniteNumber` — the same function shared by both the Codex watchdog and the downstream computer tool:

```
parseStrictFiniteNumber("0x10")   → undefined  (hex rejected ✓)
parseStrictFiniteNumber("100")    → 100        (decimal honored ✓)
parseStrictFiniteNumber("1e2")    → 100        (scientific honored ✓)
parseStrictFiniteNumber("100.5")  → 100.5      (fraction honored ✓)
parseStrictFiniteNumber(100)      → 100        (numeric honored ✓)
parseStrictFiniteNumber("abc")    → undefined  (garbage rejected ✓)
```

### Codex dependency contract

- `../codex/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs:127-142` — no field-level `duration` guard; `serde_json::Value` forwarded unchanged to OpenClaw
- `@openai/codex@0.144.4` — pinned version
- OpenClaw receives the raw JSON duration value and now parses it with the same grammar as the downstream computer tool

### Not tested

- Live Codex app-server roundtrip with real API key (the test exercises the exact same `resolveDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs` entry point and call shape as the live path at `run-attempt-server-requests.ts:191`)
- Non-computer dynamic tool timeout paths: unchanged — all 29 existing non-computer tests pass
